setting: the hill at twenty past eight in the first rain in a month, his hood down and the rain audible on the phone itself, his voice level and tired, a sentence about the ward abandoned halfway, then a long stretch of walking with nothing said, ending with a gate and the word right

her kitchen at ten to three in the morning, talking quietly so as not to wake herself further, two false starts about the boiler, then the real thing about the room being stripped back to cork; the second half is mostly the fridge cycling and her breathing and one long yawn she does not apologise for

the same hill at half eight, walking down after a night, telling her what a five second press on a lift alarm actually does and who hears it, the explanation delivered flat and complete like a handover, a bus pulling away over the last few words

a train seat with the table down, her voice under the carriage noise, starting a sentence about september three times before she gets it out, the last twelve seconds taken entirely by a tunnel so that the end of it is gone
